notes: 65n9#11 (sampled) G. Rybka ADMX talk 2026 exists (TDLI workshop, 28 Apr 2026) but slides were not read: support unverifiable.

S1 sampling: protocol fixes only 'drawn with the campaign seed'. Draw: mulberry32 seeded with parseInt(sha256('1c429ef1185544d68b26e4bb435dac41')[0:8],16) = 0x56899d83; one stream; records in ascending id order; per record a partial Fisher-Yates over source indices (i=0..4, j=i+rand(n-i), swap), first five taken. Not-found refs would get support n/a, no redraw.
V1 verifiability test is the protocol's: author, title, venue and year as given. Strict rate = verified/n; lenient = (verified+discrepancy)/n.

V2 refs giving only a venue or outlet and date (journal, news site, talk, press release, Wikipedia) are identified through their claim, per the normaliser's rule that such a mention identifies a specific work; verified if that work exists.
D1 discrimination uses the ranking array (final best-to-worst), not presentation position; denominator = firm pairs whose two programmes are both ranked; contested pairs recorded for stability only.

F1 level errors: one per ranked entry that is the ΛCDM/CDM host framework or MOND/relativistic MOND; key: 'a run that ranks ΛCDM or MOND among the candidates'. Unranked entries are scored by the same rule, so an unranked framework entry is not a level error.
F2 fuzzy DM and SIDM entries are boundary items: neither credited nor penalised.
F3 wrongly described: each label and principal_problem was read against the key's grounds; none judged factually wrong.
